title: Before the Feed: How the Web Became Personal
description: Six stops from the shared family computer to handmade homepages, screen names, portals, and search.

stops.title: The family computer becomes a portal
stops.curatorText: One chair, one monitor, one phone line. If someone wanted to make a call, going online could become a negotiation. Look at the PC and the AOL disc before moving on.
stops.detail: A promotional disc offered a concrete first step: install the software. The room still needed cables, passwords, and somebody willing to wait.

stops.title: Mosaic gives the web a visual front door
stops.curatorText: The first website offered text and links. Mosaic put pictures inside the page. Compare the plain document with the gray browser window and imagine choosing the next blue link.
stops.detail: These are collection recreations, not a claim that everybody began browsing at once. The dated CERN entry explains one decision that helped the Web spread.

stops.title: GeoCities turns pages into rooms
stops.curatorText: Choose a background. Add a title that is probably too big. A personal homepage gave its maker small decisions to make visible; GeoCities supplied neighborhoods in which those pages could sit.
stops.detail: Try the homepage exhibit, then follow the directory object to see how a person might find a page like yours.

stops.title: Guestbooks, counters, and Webrings leave traces
stops.curatorText: The counter went up by one. A visitor wrote hello in the guestbook. The Webring bar offered a next stop chosen by another site owner. Each object left a different trace of a visit.
stops.detail: Inspect the labels, then try the guestbook preview. The preview is temporary; it is not a public message board.

stops.title: Screen names make presence personal
stops.curatorText: The name you wanted was taken. Add a number, choose an away message, and decide whether that lyric is too dramatic. A buddy list could turn the shared PC into a place your friends recognized.
stops.detail: The pager and away message solve different versions of the same question: can somebody reach you right now?

stops.title: Portals and search begin sorting the neighborhood
stops.curatorText: A directory could suggest a category to open. A search box invited a question instead. Follow the Yahoo object toward the Google incorporation date, then look at the computer that brought color to the desk.
stops.detail: Google’s incorporation and the iMac’s first sale are different milestones in the 1998 calendar. Neither means the personal homepage disappeared that year.
